     6  module

     8  public import Mathlib.Data.ENNReal.Inv
     9  
    10  /-! # Hölder triples
    11  
    12  This file defines a new class: `ENNReal.HolderTriple` which takes arguments `p q r : ℝ≥0∞`,
    13  with `r` marked as a `semiOutParam`, and states that `p⁻¹ + q⁻¹ = r⁻¹`. This is exactly the
    14  condition for which **Hölder's inequality** is valid (see `MeasureTheory.MemLp.smul`).
    15  This allows us to declare a heterogeneous scalar multiplication (`HSMul`) instance on
    16  `MeasureTheory.Lp` spaces.
    17  
    18  In this file we provide many convenience lemmas in the presence of a `HolderTriple` instance.
    19  All these are easily provable from facts about `ℝ≥0∞`, but it's convenient not to be forced
    20  to reprove them each time.
    21  
    22  For convenience we also define `ENNReal.HolderConjugate` (with arguments `p q`) as an
    23  abbreviation for `ENNReal.HolderTriple p q 1`.
    24  -/
    25  
    26  public section
    27  
    28  namespace ENNReal
    29  
    30  /-- A class stating that `p q r : ℝ≥0∞` satisfy `p⁻¹ + q⁻¹ = r⁻¹`.
    31  This is exactly the condition for which **Hölder's inequality** is valid
    32  (see `MeasureTheory.MemLp.smul`).
    33  
    34  When `r := 1`, one generally says that `p q` are **Hölder conjugate**.
    35  
    36  This class exists so that we can define a heterogeneous scalar multiplication
    37  on `MeasureTheory.Lp`, and this is why `r` must be marked as a
    38  `semiOutParam`. We don't mark it as an `outParam` because this would
    39  prevent Lean from using `HolderTriple p q r` and `HolderTriple p q r'`
    40  within a single proof, as may be occasionally convenient. -/
    41  @[mk_iff]
    42  class HolderTriple (p q : ℝ≥0∞) (r : semiOutParam ℝ≥0∞) : Prop where
    43    inv_add_inv_eq_inv (p q r) : p⁻¹ + q⁻¹ = r⁻¹
    44  
    45  /-- An abbreviation for `ENNReal.HolderTriple p q 1`, this class states `p⁻¹ + q⁻¹ = 1`. -/
    46  abbrev HolderConjugate (p q : ℝ≥0∞) := HolderTriple p q 1
    47  
    48  lemma holderConjugate_iff {p q : ℝ≥0∞} : HolderConjugate p q ↔ p⁻¹ + q⁻¹ = 1 := by
    49    simp [holderTriple_iff]
    50  
    51  /-! ### Hölder triples -/
    52  
    53  namespace HolderTriple
    54  
    55  /-- This is not marked as an instance so that Lean doesn't always find this one
    56  and a more canonical value of `r` can be used. -/
    57  lemma of (p q : ℝ≥0∞) : HolderTriple p q (p⁻¹ + q⁻¹)⁻¹ where
    58    inv_add_inv_eq_inv := inv_inv _ |>.symm
    59  
    60  /- This instance causes a trivial loop, but this is exactly the kind of loop that
    61  Lean should be able to detect and avoid. -/
    62  instance symm {p q r : ℝ≥0∞} [hpqr : HolderTriple p q r] : HolderTriple q p r where
    63    inv_add_inv_eq_inv := add_comm p⁻¹ q⁻¹ ▸ hpqr.inv_add_inv_eq_inv
    64  
    65  instance instInfty (p : ℝ≥0∞) : HolderTriple p ∞ p where
    66    inv_add_inv_eq_inv := by simp
    67  
    68  instance instZero (p : ℝ≥0∞) : HolderTriple p 0 0 where
    69    inv_add_inv_eq_inv := by simp
    70  
    71  variable (p q r : ℝ≥0∞) [HolderTriple p q r]
    72  
    73  lemma inv_eq : r⁻¹ = p⁻¹ + q⁻¹ := (inv_add_inv_eq_inv ..).symm
    74  
    75  lemma unique (r' : ℝ≥0∞) [hr' : HolderTriple p q r'] : r = r' := by
    76    rw [← inv_inj, inv_eq p q r, inv_eq p q r']
    77  
    78  lemma one_div_add_one_div : 1 / p + 1 / q = 1 / r := by simpa using inv_add_inv_eq_inv ..
    79  
    80  lemma one_div_eq : 1 / r = 1 / p + 1 / q :=
    81    one_div_add_one_div p q r |>.symm
    82  
    83  lemma inv_inv_add_inv : (p⁻¹ + q⁻¹)⁻¹ = r := by
    84    si
